A activity is a BPMN element in the Flow Object - Activity category. A task that calls and executes another process (reusable subprocess). 
Purpose: A task that calls and executes another process (reusable subprocess). 
Can receive connections from: SequenceFlow Can connect to: SequenceFlow 
Common usage patterns: - Calling shared/reusable processes - Process modularization - Cross-process orchestration - Global subprocess invocation 
Key constraints: - References a separate process definition - Can pass data in/out via parameters - Creates new process instance for called process 
XML Example: <activity id="activity_1"/>

A adHocSubProcess is a BPMN element in the Flow Object - Activity category. A compound activity containing other activities, gateways, events, and data. 
Purpose: A compound activity containing other activities, gateways, events, and data. 
Can receive connections from: SequenceFlow, MessageFlow Can connect to: SequenceFlow, MessageFlow 
Common usage patterns: - Collapsed subprocess - hides internal complexity - Expanded subprocess - shows detailed flow - Event subprocess - handles exceptions or events - Reusable process components 
Key constraints: - Must have at least one Start Event - Must have at least one End Event - Can have boundary events attached - Contains complete valid process flow 
Variants: Embedded, Event, Transaction, Ad-Hoc

A boundaryEvent is a BPMN element in the Flow Object - Event category. Specifically, it is a Boundary Event. Attached to an activity boundary to handle exceptions or events during activity execution. 
Purpose: Attached to an activity boundary to handle exceptions or events during activity execution. Can connect to: SequenceFlow 
Common usage patterns: - Error Boundary Event - catch errors from activity - Timer Boundary Event - timeout handling - Message Boundary Event - receive message while activity executes - Interrupting vs Non-interrupting behavior 
Key constraints: - Must be attached to the boundary of an Activity - Cannot have incoming Sequence Flows - Must have exactly one outgoing Sequence Flow - Can be interrupting (cancels activity) or non-interrupting (activity continues) 
Variants: Message, Timer, Error, Signal, Escalation, Conditional, Cancel, Compensation, Multiple, Parallel Multiple

A event is a BPMN element in the Flow Object - Event category. Indicates where a process begins. Triggers the start of a process instance. 
Purpose: Indicates where a process begins. Triggers the start of a process instance. Can connect to: SequenceFlow 
Common usage patterns: - None Start Event - process starts immediately - Message Start Event - triggered by incoming message - Timer Start Event - triggered at specific time or interval - Signal Start Event - triggered by signal broadcast - Conditional Start Event - triggered when condition is met 
Key constraints: - Start Events must have no incoming Sequence Flows - Start Events must have at least one outgoing Sequence Flow - Only one None Start Event per Process (unless in Event Sub-Process) 
Variants: None, Message, Timer, Signal, Conditional, Error, Escalation, Compensation, Multiple, Parallel Multiple

A eventBasedGateway is a BPMN element in the Flow Object - Event category. Specifically, it is a Event-Based Gateway. Creates alternative paths based on events. Process continues on path of first event to occur. 
Purpose: Creates alternative paths based on events. Process continues on path of first event to occur. 
Can receive connections from: SequenceFlow Can connect to: IntermediateCatchEvent, ReceiveTask 
Common usage patterns: - Wait for first of multiple possible messages - Timeout handling (timer vs message race) - Event-driven routing - Responsive process patterns 
Key constraints: - Must be followed by Intermediate Catch Events or Receive Tasks - Only one event will trigger continuation - Other paths are abandoned once one event occurs - Cannot have conditions on outgoing flows 
Variants: Exclusive, Parallel, Instantiating 
XML Example: <eventBasedGateway id="eventBasedGateway_1"/>

A exclusiveGateway is a BPMN element in the Flow Object - Gateway category. Specifically, it is a Exclusive Gateway. Creates alternative paths in the process flow. Only one path is taken based on conditions. 
Purpose: Creates alternative paths in the process flow. Only one path is taken based on conditions. 
Can receive connections from: SequenceFlow Can connect to: SequenceFlow

Key constraints: - Exactly one outgoing path must be selected - Should have a default path when used for splitting - Conditions on outgoing flows must be mutually exclusive - Evaluates conditions in order until one is true 
Variants: Data-Based (XOR), Event-Based 
XML Example: <exclusiveGateway id="exclusiveGateway_1"/>

Key attributes: - implementation (optional, type: tImplementation) - operationRef (optional, type: QName) 
Can receive connections from: SequenceFlow Can connect to: SequenceFlow 
Common usage patterns: - Calling REST APIs or web services - Database operations - System integrations - Automated calculations or processing 
Key constraints: - Executed automatically by the process engine - Should specify implementation details (service endpoint, operation) - No human interaction required 
XML Example: <tServiceTask id="tServiceTask_1"/>

A tStartEvent is a BPMN element in the Flow Object - Event category. Specifically, it is a Start Event. Indicates where a process begins. Triggers the start of a process instance. 
Purpose: Indicates where a process begins. Triggers the start of a process instance. 
Key attributes: - isInterrupting (optional, type: boolean) Can connect to: SequenceFlow 
Common usage patterns: - None Start Event - process starts immediately - Message Start Event - triggered by incoming message - Timer Start Event - triggered at specific time or interval - Signal Start Event - triggered by signal broadcast - Conditional Start Event - triggered when condition is met 
Key constraints: - Start Events must have no incoming Sequence Flows - Start Events must have at least one outgoing Sequence Flow - Only one None Start Event per Process (unless in Event Sub-Process) 
Variants: None, Message, Timer, Signal, Conditional, Error, Escalation, Compensation, Multiple, Parallel Multiple 
XML Example: <tStartEvent id="tStartEvent_1" isInterrupting="true"/>

A tSubProcess is a BPMN element in the Flow Object - Activity category. A compound activity containing other activities, gateways, events, and data. 
Purpose: A compound activity containing other activities, gateways, events, and data. 
Key attributes: - triggeredByEvent (optional, type: boolean) 
Can receive connections from: SequenceFlow, MessageFlow Can connect to: SequenceFlow, MessageFlow 
Common usage patterns: - Collapsed subprocess - hides internal complexity - Expanded subprocess - shows detailed flow - Event subprocess - handles exceptions or events - Reusable process components 
Key constraints: - Must have at least one Start Event - Must have at least one End Event - Can have boundary events attached - Contains complete valid process flow 
Variants: Embedded, Event, Transaction, Ad-Hoc 
XML Example: <tSubProcess id="tSubProcess_1" triggeredByEvent="true"/>

A tTask is a BPMN element in the Flow Object - Activity category. Specifically, it is a Task. A task that executes a script in a specified scripting language. 
Purpose: A task that executes a script in a specified scripting language. 
Can receive connections from: SequenceFlow Can connect to: SequenceFlow 
Common usage patterns: - Data transformation and manipulation - Simple calculations - Variable assignments - Inline business logic 
Key constraints: - Script language must be specified - Executed by process engine - Should be simple and stateless 
XML Example: <tTask id="tTask_1"/>

A tTransaction is a BPMN element in the Other category. A specialized subprocess that groups activities into a transaction with commit/rollback semantics. 
Purpose: A specialized subprocess that groups activities into a transaction with commit/rollback semantics. 
Key attributes: - method (optional, type: tTransactionMethod) 
Can receive connections from: SequenceFlow Can connect to: SequenceFlow 
Common usage patterns: - Financial transactions - Atomic operations requiring rollback capability - Coordinated multi-party transactions - Compensatable business transactions 
Key constraints: - Supports cancel events for rollback - All activities must complete or all rollback - Can have compensation defined 
XML Example: <tTransaction id="tTransaction_1"/>

A tUserTask is a BPMN element in the Flow Object - Activity category. Specifically, it is a User Task. A task performed by a human user with the help of a software application. 
Purpose: A task performed by a human user with the help of a software application. 
Key attributes: - implementation (optional, type: tImplementation) 
Can receive connections from: SequenceFlow, MessageFlow Can connect to: SequenceFlow, MessageFlow 
Common usage patterns: - Form filling and data entry - Review and approval tasks - Manual decision making - Human interaction points in automated processes 
Key constraints: - Typically assigned to a specific user or group - May have associated forms or user interfaces - Execution waits for human completion 
XML Example: <tUserTask id="tUserTask_1"/>
